subject: Mutual Action Checklist — acceptance proofs & exit gate choreography
messages:
From: Rachel Stein <rachel.stein@medclear.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medclear.com
Date: 2026-10-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot acceptance scope & timeline (initial)

Irene — thanks again for the demo this morning. The leadership team here at MedClear wants a tight mutual action plan so we can align procurement, security, and our clinical ops teams. Two asks from our side to keep momentum: 

1) A clear list of acceptance tests (what we'll run, success thresholds, who runs them).
2) Exit gates and the minimum evidence you need for signoff (logs, dashboards, test artifacts).

Can you send a short MAP that maps each success criterion to an owner, timeline, and artifact? We have a tentative procurement review on 2026-10-29 and would like the evaluation to be materially complete before that date if possible.

Also: regulatory folks asked whether audit logs and data retention settings can be verified in a sandbox run. Happy to share more details.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Stein
Program Manager — Clinical Integrations
MedClear Health

From: irene.choi@redwood.com <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Stein <rachel.stein@medclear.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-23T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance scope & timeline (Mutual Action Plan + validation matrix)

Rachel — appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a compact MAP and a machine-readable validation matrix that ties each acceptance test to: pass threshold, evidence artifact, Redwood owner, and proposed run owner at MedClear. High level summary below so it's easy to scan at procurement: 

Executive pass criteria (short):
- Functional correctness: 95% task-level pass on the pilot prompt set across 3 runs. Evidence: validation_matrix_20261023.csv + sample outputs.
- Latency: 95th percentile per-request <= 350ms for typical 512-token flows in the sandbox (no KV cache). Evidence: latency-smoke-report.md.
- Cost predictability: token cost per 1k tokens within 10% of estimated profile during the pilot. Evidence: usage export + console cost breakdown.
- Security/compliance: audit log integrity check + KMS integration confirmed in sandbox. Evidence: audit sample + KMS handshake log.

Exit gates (must all be met for production signoff):
A. Validation matrix completed with >=95% pass for business-critical prompts (owner: MedClear QA; Redwood contact: irene.choi).
B. Latency and error-rate SLO met in two consecutive smoke runs (owner: MedClear SRE; Redwood contact: karthik.iyer).
C. Procurement terms agreed (prices & reserved capacity): signed LOI or POC SOW (owner: MedClear procurement; Redwood contact: marissa.cole).
D. Security evidence accepted: SOC2 summary + sandbox audit logs validated (owner: MedClear security; Redwood contact: security@redwood.com).

Suggested test types and who runs them:
- Functional validation (prompt set): MedClear runs against sandbox; Redwood provides seeds and scoring harness. Artifact: CSV of inputs/outputs + pass rate. Timeline: week of 10/26.
- Latency smoke: Redwood runs an instrumented smoke run; MedClear witnesses. Artifact: p95/p99 logs + flamegraph. Timeline: 10/25–10/27.
- End-to-end workflow smoke: Integrated test through your ingestion and EHR stub (MedClear owns). Timeline: 10/26–10/28.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm owners for A/B/C above by EOD 10/24.
2) We run the first validation matrix and latency smoke on 10/25.
3) We push artifacts into a shared Drive folder and Redwood will tag them in the MAP tracker.

Attachments: MedClear_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP grid), validation_matrix_20261023.csv (prompt-level test harness), latency-smoke-report-template.md (run template).

If procurement needs a single-slide summary for the 10/29 review, Marissa and I can draft one — Marissa, can you take point?

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance scope & timeline (technical clarifications)

Irene / Marissa — quick technical clarifications to make the validation matrix executable: 

1) For latency thresholds: we should define two modes — "typical" (512 tokens, warm KV cache) and "cold" (first request, empty KV). My recommendation: p95_typical <= 250ms; p95_cold <= 650ms. The 350ms number Irene suggested is fine as a cross-check, but separating warm/cold avoids ambiguity.

2) Error taxonomy: include transient (retryable) vs functional (model output fails business rules). Validation matrix should capture error class and remediation path.

3) Synthetic load for cost predictability: we'll provide a 6-hour simulated workload script to exercise tokens at expected distribution for your pilot cohort.

I'll upload a small template for the smoke-run instrumentation later today (attached: latency-smoke-report-template.md). Also tagging our infra lead if we need to open a private debug tunnel for the sandbox.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
